title: Perf Canary Workload Matrix (v0.6) — models x prompt shapes x modes
content:
Purpose
- Define the canonical workload matrix used by perf-canary runner.
- Keep it stable enough for regression detection, while still representative (prefill+decode, chat+RAG+code-ish shapes).
- This sheet is the source of truth for: model list, prompt shapes, token counts, streaming vs non-streaming modes, target regions, and expected throughput (tokens/sec) sanity ranges.

Definitions / measurement notes (for interpreting expected TPS)
- Expected tokens/sec ranges below are sanity bands for canary validation (NOT customer SLA). They’re intentionally wide to account for fleet variability.
- tokens/sec is intended as decode throughput (generated tokens / decode_time). For streaming, decode_time is (last_token_ts - first_token_ts) to avoid penalizing prefill and queueing; for non-streaming, decode_time is (response_complete_ts - first_token_ts). See also the streaming alignment fix (redwood/pr_39157).
- The canary should run with scheduler pinning enabled where available (disable experimental heuristic X) to reduce variance (see redwood/pr_39166).

Assumptions (current)
- Primary slices we expect to separate in metrics/dashboards: model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build, scheduler_mode, streaming.
- Concurrency is intentionally low (1–4) per model per region; canary traffic is rate-limited and tagged source=perf-canary.
- Prompt sets are synthetic but deterministic; no customer data.

TAB 1 — Workload Matrix (rows are the actual canary runs)
Columns:
- model: Redwood model identifier used by runner config
- prompt_shape: canonical shape name (see TAB 2)
- prompt_tokens: target prefill length (tokens)
- max_new_tokens: target decode length (tokens)
- streaming: true/false
- concurrency: parallel requests (per region per model+shape+mode)
- regions: where enabled
- gpu_sku: expected primary fleet; if mixed, we rely on slicing
- expected_tps_range: sanity band per request (decode) for a healthy system
- notes: anything that impacts variance (cache priming, warmup, etc.)

TABLE (CSV)
row_id,model,model_family,precision_profile,prompt_shape,prompt_tokens,max_new_tokens,streaming,concurrency,regions,gpu_sku,expected_tps_range,notes
1,rw/llama-3.1-8b-instruct,llama,fp16,chat_short_v1,160,256,true,2,"us-east,eu-west",H100-80GB,"650–1050","Primary high-signal canary row; stable, low variance; use for early rollout checks"
2,rw/llama-3.1-8b-instruct,llama,fp16,chat_short_v1,160,256,false,2,"us-east,eu-west",H100-80GB,"700–1150","Non-streaming control vs streaming; helps catch first-token timestamp regressions"
3,rw/llama-3.1-8b-instruct,llama,fp16,rag_2k_v1,2048,256,true,1,"us-east,eu-west",H100-80GB,"420–780","Prefill-heavy; sensitive to kernel selection + KV cache behavior; run at lower concurrency"
4,rw/llama-3.1-8b-instruct,llama,fp16,code_completion_v1,320,384,false,1,"us-east",H100-80GB,"520–900","Decode-heavy; good for catching speculative/decoder kernel changes; phase-1 only"
5,rw/llama-3.1-70b-instruct,llama,fp16,chat_short_v1,160,256,true,1,"us-east",H100-80GB,"140–240","Phase-1 anchor for large model; keep concurrency=1 to avoid queue coupling"
6,rw/llama-3.1-70b-instruct,llama,fp16,rag_2k_v1,2048,256,true,1,"us-east",H100-80GB,"95–170","Very prefill-sensitive; higher variance; only page on sustained regression + sufficient samples"
7,rw/qwen2.5-7b-instruct,qwen,fp16,chat_short_v1,160,256,true,2,"us-east,eu-west",H100-80GB,"700–1150","Secondary small-model cross-check; helps spot model-family-specific kernel/autotune drift"
8,rw/qwen2.5-32b-instruct,qwen,fp16,chat_short_v1,160,256,true,1,"eu-west",H100-80GB,"210–360","Added for EU expansion; validate region/GPU slice correctness during phase-2"
9,rw/mixtral-8x7b-instruct,mixtral,fp16,chat_short_v1,160,256,true,1,"us-east",H100-80GB,"260–480","MoE routing variance; keep single concurrency; good for catching scheduling/batching heuristic changes"
10,rw/mistral-7b-instruct,mistral,fp16,chat_short_v1,160,256,true,2,"eu-west",A100-80GB,"320–600","EU has partial A100 fleet; this row ensures dashboards split gpu_sku cleanly"
11,rw/mistral-7b-instruct,mistral,fp16,rag_2k_v1,2048,256,false,1,"eu-west",A100-80GB,"210–430","Non-streaming prefill-heavy on A100; tends to show kernel regression earlier than H100"
12,rw/llama-3.1-8b-instruct,llama,int8w,chat_short_v1,160,256,true,2,"us-east",H100-80GB,"800–1250","Quantized profile smoke-check (if enabled); should be clearly faster than fp16; disable if it introduces too much variance"

TAB 1.1 — Phase coverage summary (operational)
- Phase 1 (us-east): rows 1–6, 9, 12 (2–3 ‘page-worthy’ anchors: rows 1,2,5)
- Phase 2 (eu-west): rows 1–3, 7–8, 10–11 (focus: region rollout + gpu_sku slice correctness)

Guardrails / stability requirements (what we consider a good canary row)
- p95 latency CV should be < ~10% over a normal workday outside deploy windows (rule of thumb; measured after warmup).
- tokens/sec should not show step changes correlated with cache warmups; if it does, add/extend cache priming or increase warmup discard window.
- Avoid prompt shapes that trigger tool-calling / structured output parsing differences (unless we explicitly want that slice).

TAB 2 — Prompt shapes (canonical definitions)
Notes:
- Prompt shapes refer to deterministic templates in perf-canary repo prompt set loader (perf-canary/pr_102). Token counts are targets; actual tokens may vary slightly by tokenizer/model.

TABLE (CSV)
prompt_shape,description,template_notes,target_prompt_tokens,target_new_tokens,why_included,variance_risk
chat_short_v1,"Short multi-turn chat w/ a small system prompt + 2 user turns","Deterministic names/dates; no external calls",160,256,"Primary real-world-ish baseline; stable across models","Low"
rag_2k_v1,"RAG-style prompt with ~2k tokens of ‘retrieved context’ + short question","Context is synthetic paragraphs w/ fixed seed; include separators",2048,256,"Prefill-heavy; catches attention kernel regressions + KV/cache changes","Medium (prefill sensitive)"
code_completion_v1,"Code completion: function stub + docstring + partial implementation","Use stable language (Python); no randomness",320,384,"Decode-heavy; catches decoder kernel changes and scheduler fairness",Medium
summarize_4k_v1,"Long document summarization: 4k input tokens + constrained output","Synthetic article text; fixed headings",4096,256,"Stress long-context prefill; use sparingly due to high cost",High (fleet contention)"

Open questions / TODO
- Decide if we want a dedicated ‘streaming-first-token’ micro-row (e.g., prompt_tokens=32, max_new_tokens=32, streaming=true) purely for TTFT/stream start regressions. Currently not included to avoid over-expanding matrix.
- Confirm whether eu-west H100 coverage is sufficient to make H100-only expected_tps_range meaningful; if not, we should add explicit A100/H100 parallel rows (same model/shape) and rely on slicing.
- Confirm final list of “page-worthy anchors” with SRE (Sean) once we finish backtesting (ENG-2855).

Changelog
- 2026-02-07: Added explicit A100 rows for eu-west (rows 10–11) after early slice confusion in dashboard mockups.
- 2026-02-03: Split streaming vs non-streaming for llama-8b baseline (rows 1–2) to validate tokens/sec alignment.
- 2026-01-24: Added scheduler pinning note + lowered concurrency for large models to reduce coupling.
